**AX. L67as -- LIVE READER AUDIT (owner-approved step 2 of the 2026-09-15 strategy plan): the HP-bar reader cannot supply unit HP live (3.6% of detections), the velocity reader can.** Measured on session `20260912_152220` (run18, 5 matches), 3,650 in-match frames at 4.0 Hz, 9,628 detections, offline replay of recorded frames -- no live game touched. Tool: `icebow/tools/live_reader_audit.py` (new); full numbers + limitations `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/reader_audit/report.md`.

***RETRACTION (my own, from AW).*** AW proposal (3) named **unit HP as the first live-matched feature to add to S1 v7**, on the assumption that `detect_obs.read_hp_frac` was a working reader whose error merely needed measuring. **Contradicted (c):** it returns a bar on **3.6% of detections** (n=9,628) and on **22.7% of tracks** (n=643; enemy 16.2%, mine 34.0%). There is no error distribution to model because there is almost no signal -- feeding it to S1 would supply the constant 1.0 it already sends, plus noise on 3.6% of tokens. Unit HP is **not** an available live feature today; it is a detector project (a bar-segmentation head), not a wiring job.

*HP-bar reader, what the audit does establish (a).* Where it does fire it is not obviously wrong: at-deploy (our own PLAY matched to our own new unit within 1.5 s / 0.15 frame-radius; 112 of 166 plays matched, 54 with no own unit detected) the first read has **median 1.000, 97.3% >= 0.90, 0.9% < 0.70** -- a freshly deployed unit reads full, as it must. Jitter between reads ~0.2 s apart: **median 0.000** (n=51). Read rate by class is highest on big/wide sprites (lava_hound 9.4%, x_bow 7.3%, knight 5.4%) and near zero on small or spell classes (royal_recruits 1.2%, earthquake 0.0%), consistent with a reader that needs a wide unoccluded bar.

*The one real anomaly (a, unexplained).* **20.2%** of consecutive found-read pairs on the same track **increase** by more than 0.10 (n=178). Nothing in either deck heals or shields, so HP must be monotone non-increasing. Either the reader is noisy where it does fire, or track identity is being swapped between two units of the same class. The audit cannot separate these from self-consistency alone. **Not established:** which. A labelled slice would settle it; not worth running unless the reader is rebuilt.

*Velocity reader (a).* **89.0%** of tracks (n=643) live long enough (>= 0.5 s) to report a velocity -- i.e. movement is available for the large majority of units, unlike HP. Per-class median speed on straight moving segments tracks the published constants but **overshoots them by a consistent 1.08-1.20x across ~15 unrelated classes** (skeletons 1.76 vs 1.5; knight 1.19 vs 1.0; bats 2.28 vs 2.0; firecracker 1.73 vs 1.5; lumberjack 2.28 vs 2.0). A shared bias across unrelated cards points at one shared cause -- most likely the flat `TILE_X`/`TILE_Y` linear scale the audit borrows from `hero_ability.py`, which ignores the perspective warp `actions.BoardWarp` corrects for taps. **(b) untested:** re-deriving the scale or applying BoardWarp per point should collapse the cluster toward 1.0; nobody has tried.
- *Heading is the weak half (a).* Median |angle change| between consecutive moving velocity estimates on the same track: **43.7 deg** (n=5,365). Speed is usable; instantaneous direction is not, without smoothing over several frames.
- *Stationary buildings report motion (a).* tesla 0.41, x_bow 0.30 tiles/s -- a floor of pure tracking jitter, and a useful scale for how much of any small measured speed is noise.

*A charge-status lead (b, untested, and the first evidence that the owner's "status effects" gap may be partly readable).* The classes sitting far ABOVE the 1.08-1.20 bias cluster are disproportionately the charge/dash cards: **prince 2.01x** (2.01 vs 1.0 tiles/s -- the in-game charge is ~2x base), dark_prince 1.63x, mega_knight 1.57x, goblin_giant 1.50x, battle_ram 1.37x. If that is charge and not bias, a per-unit speed-vs-card-constant ratio is a **derived charging flag from data we already compute**, needing no new detector. Caveats that stop this being a finding: lava_hound also reads 1.38x and does not charge; n is 10-49 per class; and the shared warp bias is unquantified, so part of every ratio is instrument. The measurement that settles it: correct the warp, then re-read the ratio time series within single prince tracks -- a charge should appear as a step, not a constant offset.

*What this changes (b).* The S1 v7 feature list from AW reorders: **movement/velocity in, unit HP out** (until a bar detector exists). Order now: (1) velocity/heading over 2-3 frames, after the warp fix; (2) static card stats per token (hitpoints, range) from `cards_stats.json`, which need no reader at all; (3) a derived charge flag if the ratio lead survives; (4) unit HP only behind a real bar-segmentation head. Princess tower HP is already live and real (AW).

*What this does NOT establish.* No ground truth exists on a live screen -- every number above is a self-consistency check against a game rule (own-play identity, no-heal monotonicity, a published speed constant), so a reader wrong in a way consistent with those rules passes undetected. `read_hp_frac` returns exactly 1.0 both for "no bar" and "full bar", so the read rate is a proxy. The detector's own recall is a separate unmeasured variable beneath every number here: a unit never boxed contributes no evidence to any check. Towers were assumed alive throughout (no offline tower-HP reader), which cannot affect the at-deploy check.

Report MAE/bias per condition, by match phase. No live play needed.

Something breaks the match for continuously visible units; **unresolved**, and the exact experiment is cheap (below).

A real detector's errors persist across frames (AX: 89% of live tracks survive >= 0.5 s), so the true live error lies between A_wl (2.35) and B (5.90). Where in that range is unmeasured and cannot be measured against truth live.

*Instrument note (a).* A+ == A to full precision: the engine BoardState carries no spells (`compact_raw` drops effects/projectiles), so the spell path was a no-op here; the spell blind spot is measured through the delivered-play ledger instead.

*What this does NOT establish.* The re-charge code path; the live error itself (bounded, not measured); what any fix would yield; anything about tower/king HP.

*V2.1 under perfect detection (a).* The four rules (R4 singleton re-sighting, R5 body-occupancy absorption, R6 SPAWNS additions, R7 r_spawn 0.12) took over-billing from V2's +32% to **+6.6%** and bias from -1.20 to **-0.14**: essentially unbiased, MAE 1.51, within 1 elixir on 53% of ticks (V1: 36%). The residual classes named in BE are closed. **This is the ceiling for the owner's drop-in-animation idea** -- engine first-appearance IS perfect deploy detection, so a perfect animation detector tops out near MAE 1.5 *without* the whitelist, and 2.33 with it.

***The whitelist blind spot is now the dominant live error (a), and fixing the estimator made it worse in relative terms.*** A_wl under-bills by **34.5%** and reads **+1.69 elixir too high**. V1's A_wl looked "accurate" (bias +0.74) only because two ~3x errors cancelled; as the over-billing shrank, the 34.4%-of-plays blind spot (BD: bases outside `detector_cards`, plus every spell) stopped being masked. **This is a detector-coverage/config problem, not an algorithm problem**, and it is now the biggest single lever on the live path.

*The tracker-input design (a).* Billing once per TeamTracker-confirmed track beats billing on raw detections under every noise model: memoryless **2.68 vs 5.77**, SHORT **3.88 vs 5.58**, LONG **3.46 vs 4.27** (live-reachable `_tt_wl` variants). Over-billing collapses from 13.0x to +10.9% on memoryless noise. **The design is directionally right.** But the live-reachable estimate ranges **2.68-3.88** across the three noise models -- a 1.2-elixir spread that is model choice, not measurement, exactly the ambiguity the sweep was built to expose.

*Two findings I did not predict (a).* (1) **The raw estimator gets BETTER as noise persists** (5.77 memoryless -> 5.58 SHORT -> 4.27 LONG). Mechanism (b): the per-sample FP rate is matched across settings, so longer-lived phantoms mean FEWER DISTINCT phantom objects, hence fewer spurious first-sightings to bill. (2) Consequently **the idealised tracker HURTS under LONG persistence** (4.62 vs the raw 4.27): a phantom that survives 8 samples clears min_hits and is billed once, while the raw estimator's own tracker was already absorbing it. Only the whitelist rescues the tracker there (3.46). So the tracker's advantage is largest exactly where noise is least persistent -- and a real detector's noise persistence is unmeasured.

*What this does NOT establish.* Which noise model resembles the real detector -- AX measured 89% of live tracks surviving >= 0.5 s and 43.7 deg heading instability, which anchors neither L_miss nor L_fp; the SHORT/LONG constants remain judgment calls. The live error of the tracker design is therefore **bounded 2.68-3.88 by model choice**, not measured. Nothing here says what MAE is good enough: the +16/+26 of BC was measured for the TRUE opponent elixir, and no run has yet fed the model an estimate of any accuracy. Single checkpoint/tau/seed; engine ghosts, not live play.

*The decisive next experiment (b, not started).* This instrument can answer the only question that matters. `e1_eval --noise-off opp_elixir` supplies TRUE opponent elixir and measured **+16 / +26 winrate**. Add a mode that supplies the ESTIMATOR's value instead (V2.1 fed by tracker-confirmed dets, i.e. `B_tt_wl` quality, MAE ~2.7) and re-run the arm on both slices. That converts "MAE 2.7" into "recovers X of the +16" and is the precondition for v7: if a 2.7-MAE estimate recovers most of the effect, wire it live and train v7 on that error; if it recovers none, the whole opponent-elixir line closes with a measured negative and the 40-point gap must be attacked elsewhere. Cost ~1.5 h engine. Secondary, cheaper: the whitelist/spell coverage gap (A_wl's -34.5%) is now worth more than any further estimator rule.

Read-only audit (scout O21) + lead follow-up measurements; fix in commit 11c6e2f. **Data caveat throughout: tonight's session was NOT recorded -- the newest on disk is 20260912_152220 -- so every number below comes from run12b / run18 / run20 stdout logs, i.e. week-old play, NOT the session the owner actually watched.**

| owner's observation | verdict |
|---|---|
| "every X-Bow was offensive" | **(a) CONFIRMED -- 30/30.** My contrary claim RETRACTED, see below |
| dead-lane bows in overtime | **(a) mechanism found in code, FIXED (11c6e2f)** |
| rocket badly underused | **(a) CONFIRMED** -- ~1% of plays; and it is NOT gated, see below |
| never a rocket+tornado combo | **(a) CONFIRMED** -- zero pairs within 3 s |
| never finishes a low-HP princess | **NOT RECOVERABLE** -- tower HP is not logged per play |
| "reaction time is slowing down" | **(c) contradicted as stated** -- cadence is stable; it is pause share |
| "forced towards targeting the king tower" | **(c) contradicted** -- no such code exists |
| "plays much further forward in overtime" | **not supported on available data, but the data is the wrong session** |

***RETRACTION (mine, owner-corrected).*** I reported the model's X-Bows as "4.4% of plays, ALL defensive, zero offensive", using a `y > 0.5` threshold **I invented**. The owner replied that every X-Bow he watched was offensive and reached the enemy tower. He was right. The code defines the boundary itself: `play.xbow_forward_board_y: 0.58` (config.yaml:1369 -- "the live X-Bow assists treat a bow as OFFENSIVE only forward of this BOARD depth"). Re-measured against 0.58: **all 30 X-Bows across run20 (6), run18 (11) and run12b (13) sat at board y = 0.61 -- every one forward of the line, i.e. offensive, zero defensive.** X-Bow is precisely the card where own-half does not mean defensive: siege range ~11.5 tiles puts the standard offensive placement behind the river on your own side. Section C of `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/behaviour/O21_audit.md` is annotated retracted in place so it cannot be cited. Lesson recorded: read the threshold the code defines before inventing one.

*1. Reaction time (a).* Median inter-decision gap **~4.2-4.3 s, stable across all three runs** -- no trend in decision cadence. What reads as slowness is **pause share**: v6lat tau 0.27 **27%** -> v6aug tau 0.27 **35%** -> v6aug tau 0.24 **49%** of match time in >10 s pauses (5cs.99 AU/AV). The owner has been running **tau 0.24**, the worst of the three. The gate no-ops for long stretches and then acts at normal speed. **This is the single best-evidenced change available to the live command: tau 0.27, not 0.24.** Not separated from a possible late-game effect of rising unit counts (b).

*2. Rocket -- NOT gated, simply not chosen (a).* Counted decisions where rocket was in the tap hand AND elixir >= 6, against rockets actually played: run20 39/1, run18 37/1, run12b 52/2. **128 opportunities, 4 rockets, under 3%.** Neither the affordability mask nor the gate is the cause. The model does not select it. That is card selection, which imitation training determines, so it is **not a live-path fix and not fixable overnight**. It also explains the absent rocket+tornado combo without a separate theory: a two-card combo cannot appear when one half is played once per match. The existing rocket assists (`weaker_princess_cell`, `pump_rocket_cell`) are irrelevant here -- an assist that aims a rocket cannot fire when no rocket is played.

*3. King targeting (c).* No `king_tower_cell` exists anywhere. play.py:343-344 documents deliberate king avoidance ("a spell that reaches their king wakes it") and masks cells accordingly. The owner's hypothesis that bridge-shoving comes from being forced toward the king is **not supported by the code**. Match state (1-0 vs 1-1) IS tracked by `TowerTracker` but never emitted to the log, so his tower-doctrine rule cannot be audited against play from these logs at all -- a logging gap, not a behaviour finding.

*4. Overtime forwardness -- untested, not refuted.* Only run12b reached overtime (12 non-X-Bow plays past t=180 s; run18 never did, run20 had one). Median board-y **0.550 regular vs 0.550 overtime**; enemy-half placements 10% vs 17%, a two-play difference on n=12. The owner watched several overtime matches tonight and none were recorded, so this measures the wrong session at a useless sample size.

***The one real live-path defect, and it is fixed (a, commit 11c6e2f).*** play.py ran `xbow_target_lane_cell` -- the anti-dead-lane fix written after the owner's **2026-08-16** report of exactly this -- and then ran `xbow_lock_cell` **unconditionally**. The lock took `enemy_anchors[:2]` with no aliveness argument and snapped to the **nearer** princess, dead or alive, so the lane correction was overwritten two lines later by a function that did not know the tower was down. Fix: optional `enemy_alive=None` on `xbow_lock_cell` (None reproduces HEAD exactly, so env.py's positional call and therefore **training** are untouched); dead princesses dropped from the candidate set **before** the nearest-lane pick; empty set returns None, leaving the model's cell -- **never redirected toward the king**, per the owner's doctrine. Index mapping verified before relying on it (`enemy_alive[i]` corresponds to `enemy_a[i]`, reward.py:653-681). 26 tests green including a precondition test asserting the pre-fix default *would* have picked the dead lane, and a test running play.py's full lane-fix -> lock sequence with one tower down.

*Structural finding worth keeping (a).* The doctrine assists are NOT bypassed by the student, as first appeared: `student_live.py` calls none of them, but play.py:1045-1047 takes the **student's** chosen `(card, cell)` and :1052+ post-processes that cell (weaker-princess snap, king-safe pump rocket, X-Bow lane + lock + pocket). The doctrine layer already applies to the deployed policy, and all of it is enabled by default (`xbow_pocket_after_tower: True`, aim radii 0.10-0.12). So these complaints are mostly **not** "the model must be retrained to learn placement" -- placement is already corrected. What training governs is **which card gets played at all**, which is exactly where rocket fails.

*What this does NOT establish.* Anything about tonight's play (unrecorded). Whether the owner's tower doctrine (1-0 defend / 1-1 take the other princess) is followed -- match state is not logged, so it is unauditable today. Whether the dead-lane fix changes live behaviour (engine ghosts do not exercise the X-Bow assists the way live does; it is verified by unit test only). hogeq carries the identical dead-lane defect, untouched (its play.py has diverged 424 lines).

*Owed next, cheapest first (b).* (1) **Record the next live session** -- three of four complaints are unauditable without it. (2) **Emit match state and phase to the log** (tower alive/dead, overtime flag): without them the owner's doctrine rule and the overtime claim can never be measured. (3) Rocket selection is a **training** change, not a live one -- and per 5cs.99 BG the first thing training should carry is the measured opponent-elixir error, so these should be one retrain, not two. (4) Port the dead-lane fix to hogeq. (5) `test_xbow_pocket.py` still pins source text via `src.index()` -- the third such brittle test found tonight.


**BI. L67bw -- THE OPPONENT-ELIXIR FEED REPLICATES ON A DISJOINT SLICE (+8), BUT BELOW THE BAR I PRE-REGISTERED (0.82). The live flags are wired to exactly the condition measured.** Slice 2 = held-out entries **100:200**, sharing no entry with slice 1 (0:100). Checkpoint `s1_icebow_v6aug_s1.pt` -- the one actually deployed live -- tau 0.27, seeds 0, shard 0/1, both arms run by `pipeline.opp_est_audit` in the SAME batch (`chain_opp_feed_v6aug_s2.ps1`), so the control and the estimate arm differ in one thing only: whether the V2 estimate is written into the policy's `BoardState.opp_elixir`.

| arm | entries | winrate | entry-weighted CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ctrl_v6aug_s2` (`--feed-opp-elixir off`) | 100:200 | **0.71** (71/100) | 0.62-0.80 |
| `feed_est_v6aug_s2` (`estimated`, `--feed-noise live`) | 100:200 | **0.79** (79/100) | 0.71-0.87 |
| slice 1 control (carried, e1_eval `attrib\e2_v6aug_s1_tau027`) | 0:100 | 0.74 (74/100) | 0.65-0.82 |
| slice 1 estimate (carried, L67bv) | 0:100 | 0.85 (85/100) | 0.78-0.92 |

*Paired, measured this loop (a).* The two slice-2 arms matched **100/100 on (tag, k)** -- zero unmatched either way, so this is a genuinely paired design. **16 matches flipped loss->win, 8 flipped win->loss, 76 unchanged, net +8.** Slice 1 was +11 (flips 16/5, carried from BG/L67bv and measured against an anchor produced by a *different module*, `e1_eval`, so its flip count is weaker evidence than slice 2's same-module pairing). Pooled over both slices: control **145/200 = 0.725**, estimate **164/200 = 0.82**, delta **+9.5**.

***I missed my own pre-registered bar and am not moving it (c, against my stated prediction).*** Before the run I wrote: *"slice 1 gave 0.85 vs 0.74 = +11, so the slice-2 estimate arm needs roughly 0.82 to replicate."* It landed **0.79**. That is 3 points short of the number I committed to. The honest reading is not "replicated" without qualification and not "failed": **the sign and the rough magnitude held on a disjoint slice (+11 then +8), the paired flips are strongly positive (16/8) and the control CIs overlap the estimate CIs in both slices.** A single 100-match arm cannot separate +8 from +11 -- the instrument's own band at this n is wider than that difference (HANDOFF §7: winrate is not a discriminator at affordable n; +-12pp at n=16, and the entry-weighted CI here is +-9pp at n=100). What the two slices together establish is a positive effect of roughly +8 to +11, not a point value.

*Estimator quality on this slice (a).* Live-reachable condition B_tt_wl (V2, billed once per TeamTracker-confirmed track, restricted to live's `detector_cards`): **MAE 2.585, bias +0.163, |err|<=2.0 on 48.9% of ticks**. Perfect-detection ceiling on the same ticks (A+): MAE 1.405. The raw live billing path (B) remains MAE 5.570 with bias **-5.559** -- i.e. V1's pinned-low failure is reproduced on this slice too. So the +8 is bought with an estimate roughly 2.6 elixir off, not a near-perfect one, which is the robustness result from BG holding on new entries.

***The live wiring matches the measured condition (a, verified by reading, not assumed).*** With `play.opp_elixir_v2: true` (config.yaml:1291) and `play.student_opp_elixir: true` (config.yaml:1297): play.py:428 constructs `OpponentElixirEstimatorV2`; play.py:613-615 bills from **TeamTracker-confirmed tracks** (`_ploop.bill_confirmed(_opp_bill, detector_cards)`, fallback `_opp_elixir_v2_bill(...)` filtered by `d.base in detector_cards`); play.py:617 updates V2 from that billed list; play.py:975 passes `_opp_elx._est` to the student iff `_student_opp_elixir`. That is condition **B_tt_wl fed to the policy** -- the same object the experiment injected. Both flags are already enabled in the committed config.

*What this does NOT establish.* **No live winrate was measured, at all.** The 200 matches are engine ghosts replaying recorded opponents, not live ladder play. The estimator's input in the experiment is the ghost detection log degraded by the measured live noise model; in live play its input is the real detector on real frames, whose miss/FP behaviour is only *modelled* here. Nothing here says the +8 survives to ladder -- it says the policy uses a ~2.6-MAE opponent-elixir number to win more engine matches, robustly, on two disjoint slices. It also says nothing about the four behaviour complaints (BH); this feed does not touch card selection, and rocket underuse is untouched by it.

*Cost.* Two 100-match arms, ~02:12Z-03:02Z, engine stopped clean afterwards (qemu 0, 8.3 GB free).


**BJ. L67bx -- THE BOARD-Y DIRECTION SETTLED FROM CODE THAT COMPUTES IT, AND TWO MORE OF MY CLAIMS RETRACTED: the 0.58 cut is correct, and the fix I shipped last night is probably inert.** The owner asked whether his defensive-X-Bow-when-ahead issue was addressed. This question has now produced three different answers from me, so I re-derived it from geometry code rather than from comments or memory. Full evidence in `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/behaviour/O23_xbow_geometry.md`.

***Direction (a, settled).*** **Larger board y = closer to OUR tower; forward = DECREASING y.** From `pipeline/obs_contract.py:32-35`, which computes the literals: enemy towers at y 0.094/0.203, ours at 0.797/0.906, river 0.5. Confirmed independently in frame space by the measured `config.yaml:1074-1075` and by `actions.py:84-85`. The board->frame warp (`actions.py:88,111-116`) is strictly monotone increasing, so the sign cannot flip between spaces.

***RETRACTION 1 (c, mine).*** I wrote that `xbow_forward_board_y: 0.58` "appears mis-set". **It is not.** A bow at board 0.61 maps to frame 0.5064 against the cut's 0.4890, so `cy >= defense_y` is True and all three assists (`reward.py:445-446`, `492-493`, `539-540`) return `None` = "defensive bow, leave it alone". 0.58 was chosen deliberately so the pro row (0.604-0.609) lands on the defensive side, fixing a run15 regression where 16 of 17 X-Bows were shoved to the bridge (`play.py:318-322`); `icebow/tests/test_xbow_live_depth.py:62-66` pins that intent. Both the owner and the code are right about different things: the owner's bows ARE offensive in EFFECT (siege range ~11.5 tiles, `geometry_reward.py:34`, reaches the tower from your own half), while the code's word "offensive" means only "forward of 0.58, so the assists may reposition it".

***RETRACTION 2 (b, mine, and it matters most).*** **Commit 11c6e2f -- the dead-lane fix I shipped last night -- is probably INERT on the live path.** `play.py:1084-1086` is an `if`/`elif` on a walrus: the pocket branch fires only when `xbow_pocket_cell` returns non-None, which requires an enemy princess actually down (`reward.py:374-382`). So with a tower down the pocket overrides placement wholesale and the lane/lock/depth chain **never runs**; with no tower down the chain runs but every assist returns `None` for a bow at 0.61 before the aliveness filter is ever reached. The fix is correct code with 26 passing tests and it cannot affect the bows the model actually plays. It is not harmful, it is just not doing anything. I reported it to the owner as a fix for behaviour he had reported twice; that was overstated.

***The real conflict, and it is the owner's call (a in code, judgement not mine).*** Tower state DOES gate placement -- my earlier "nothing consumes TowerTracker for placement" was wrong. `play.py:1084-1091` calls `xbow_pocket_cell(tower_tracker.enemy_alive, ...)` and, once an enemy princess is down, **overrides the model's cell to board y 0.391 -- the ENEMY half** (`xbow_pocket_after_tower: true`, `config.yaml:1371/1373`). That is the exact state in the owner's doctrine ("ahead on towers -> defend until the match ends") and the code does the opposite. It is a pro-derived play, not a bug, so the two doctrines genuinely conflict and the owner decides. **Asked via Discord with `--questions`; no code changed.**

*But it is rare (a, measured this loop, and it kills my own hypothesis).* Scanned all 19 `live_run*_utf8.log`: `[assist] XBOW pocket` fires **exactly twice in the entire archive**, both in run18, both with one enemy princess down and the side matching the dead tower (`enemy_alive [True,False,True]` -> right, `[False,True,True]` -> left). Every other run: zero. So the pocket executes correctly but far too rarely to explain the owner's report of repeatedly playing forward in overtime -- I floated it as the mechanism and the count refutes that. **The cause of the forward overtime play remains unknown and unmeasured.**

*Also corrected (a).* No crown-count or damage-lead gate on placement exists anywhere in the live path; the only score-like signal is per-tower HP in `xbow_target_lane_cell` (`reward.py:460-465`, `hp_margin` 0.10).

*What this does NOT establish.* Why the model plays forward in overtime -- the pocket is now largely ruled out by rarity. Whether 11c6e2f is inert in practice as opposed to by code reading. Whether the pocket is rare because the 1-0 state is rare at X-Bow time or because it was disabled in older runs -- not separated. Anything about the session the owner watched, which is **still unrecorded** -- that remains the single highest-value cheap action outstanding.


**BK. L67by -- OWNER RULING: the X-Bow pocket assist is OFF, and every tap now stamps match state. Two live-path changes, both revertible in one line each.** Owner 2026-09-18, deciding the BJ conflict: *"the pro derived play clearly does not apply at 10,000 trophies, so go with A: switch it off. I want to see how the model behaves in overtime with the switch off, then based on the observations we can make more targeted fixes."* Committed f3cf655.

Match state on every tap (play.py:1208), LOGGING ONLY.* Each `[student] TAP` line now also carries `ot=<0|1> ot_s=<seconds into overtime> enemy_alive=[..] mine_alive=[..]`. **This is the gap that made three of the owner's four complaints unmeasurable**: overtime is marked nowhere in the log, and tower state is tracked by `TowerTracker` but never emitted. Decisions are untouched -- the block only prints, wrapped in `try/except` so a logging line can never kill the live loop (degrades to `ot=?`). **Appended AFTER `wall=` deliberately:** `tap_audit.py`'s regex ends at `wall=([\d:.]+)` and uses `re.match`, so trailing fields cannot break it -- **verified, not assumed**: old and new lines parse to identical groups.

It concerns an `env.*` training value, not the `play.*` config touched here. Left alone rather than bundling an unrelated fix (one change per experiment); now owed. Tau 0.27 not 0.24 -- pause share 27% / 35% / **49%** (BH). The opponent-elixir feed is the evidence-backed half (BI: +8 replicated on a disjoint slice); the pocket switch is the owner's doctrine call, expected to be near-inert on its own.

*hogeq untouched.* It carries the same flag (`hogeq/config/config.yaml:1092`) and keeps it ON: that deck has no X-Bow, so the assist is inert there.

*What this does NOT establish.* Nothing about live effect -- both changes are unmeasured in live play; that is what the owner's overnight run is for. Whether the forward-overtime behaviour he reported changes at all (I expect not, from the 2-firing count). **BL. L67bz -- THE DEAD-LANE BUG, FOUND AT LAST: the rule that forbids it was gated behind a depth cut that every real bow sits behind. Two of my previous "fixes" were inert for this one reason, and I can now name the line.** Owner reported it a **third** time (2026-08-16, then twice on 2026-09-18): *"It had several opportunities to attack the right lane. it kept putting xbows in the dead left lane. your fix did nothing."* He is right. Commit f-series L67bz.

***The cause (a, exact line).*** `reward.xbow_target_lane_cell` rule 1 is literally *"NEVER bow a dead lane"*. Line 445 gated **every** rule behind `if len(princesses) < 2 or cy >= defense_y: return None`, on the assumption that a dead-lane bow is an OFFENSIVE one. It is not. Every bow the model plays sits at **board y 0.61 -> frame 0.5064** against the cut's **0.4890** -- **behind** it. The function returned `None` before rule 1 could execute. **The dead-lane rule has never once fired on a bow the model actually plays**, in either deck, since the day it was written for the owner's original report.

*This retroactively explains both failed fixes (a).* (1) **11c6e2f (O22)** added `enemy_alive` filtering to `xbow_lock_cell` at lines 487-491 -- and that function returns `None` at line **492** for exactly these bows. It filtered a candidate list discarded on the next line. BJ called it "probably inert"; it is inert, and the mechanism is now named rather than suspected. (2) The **L67by pocket flip** removed the only assist still moving these bows at all, which is why the owner saw it get *worse* overnight.

***The fix (a).*** `xbow_target_lane_cell(..., dead_lane_any_depth=False)`. When True, **rule 1 runs at any depth**; an X-Bow reaches a tower from your own half (siege ~11.5 tiles), so its LANE matters whatever its row. **Rule 2 (weaker tower) deliberately stays offensive-only** -- it is an attacking preference, not a correctness fix, and chasing HP could drag a genuinely defensive bow off the lane it was placed to defend. **Default False reproduces the old behaviour exactly, so env.py's positional call and therefore TRAINING are untouched** (the same backward-compatible pattern as O22). play.py passes it from new `play.xbow_dead_lane_any_depth` (default true). **REVERT: set that flag false.**

*Instrumented on purpose (b -> verifiable).* Added `[assist] XBOW dead-lane cell X->Y enemy_alive [..]` to the live log. Two of my last three claims about this code were wrong; the next run should **prove** whether the rule fires rather than resting on my reasoning. If the owner reports dead-lane bows again and this line is absent, the correction is still not reaching the placement; if the line is present and he still sees them, the problem is elsewhere (card selection or the model's own cell).

***RETRACTION (c, mine, less than a day old).*** I told the owner the pocket assist was **"near-inert -- 2 firings across 19 recorded runs"** and predicted little or no visible change from switching it off. **The denominator was wrong.** The feature only landed **2026-09-12 (563e4dc)**, so only run18 and run20 could ever have fired it -- and **run18 fired on 2 of its 11 bows, ~18%**. I diluted a real rate across 17 runs that could not possibly fire it, then used that to reassure him. He saw the difference immediately. The lesson is narrow and repeatable: **when counting how often a feature fires, the denominator is runs that HAD the feature.**

*Full suite after the fix (a).* **1525 passed, 21 skipped, 1 failed** in 476 s. The single failure is the PRE-EXISTING `test_xbow_into_push.py::test_the_clamped_frontmost_ROW_counts_as_forward` (`0.5625 >= env.xbow_front 0.625`), proven pre-existing TWICE tonight: it fails identically against the restored pre-edit config, and it was already failing in the 1516-pass run made before this fix existed. **No new regressions** -- the +9 passes are exactly the new dead-lane test class. That broken test is an `env.*` training assertion, still owed, deliberately not bundled into a firefight.

*What this does NOT establish.* That the fix works **live** -- it is verified by 26 unit tests and by reasoning about play.py's sequence (lane moves the cell; `xbow_lock_cell` and `xbow_offense_depth_cell` both return None at this depth, so neither can undo it), **not** by live observation. Whether the owner's bows are in the dead lane because of placement at all, as opposed to the model choosing that cell for reasons the assists then fail to correct. Whether the pocket should go back on (owner ruled it off; the dead-lane fix now serves his stated doctrine better than the pocket did). hogeq carries the identical defect, untouched.


**BM. L67ca -- THE STRUCTURAL FINDING BEHIND MONTHS OF FAILED X-BOW FIXES: the model plays every X-Bow at one fixed depth, and that depth is exactly where the entire X-Bow assist layer switches itself off.** Measured from the three recent live logs after the owner said he was closing the project. This is ONE finding, not the three separate assist bugs I have been reporting.

***1. The X-Bow is the ONLY degenerate card in the deck (a).*** Placement entropy per card, across run20 / run18 / run12b:

| card | unique cells | entropy (bits) |
|---|---|---|
| the_log | 12 / 19 / 22 | 3.50 / 3.92 / 4.25 |
| skeletons | 9 / 16 / 17 | 2.78 / 3.72 / 3.74 |
| ice_wizard | 7 / 20 / 13 | 2.50 / 4.21 / 3.04 |
| tornado | 9 / 12 / 18 | 3.17 / 3.27 / 4.00 |
| **x_bow** | **3 / 5 / 2** | **1.25 / 1.97 / 0.62** |

**The policy is NOT broken in general** -- every other card shows real situational spread (3-4 bits). The X-Bow, the deck's win condition, is a near-constant: in run12b it played **84.6% of its 13 bows into a single cell**, with 2 unique cells total.

***2. Those cells are a binary lane pick at ONE fixed depth (a).*** Decoded: cell **254 = board x 0.139 (LEFT), y 0.604**; cell **267 = board x 0.861 (RIGHT), y 0.604**. Same row, mirrored columns. run20 and run18 sat mostly on LEFT (254), run12b 84.6% on RIGHT (267). The model picks a side, largely sticks to it for the run, and **never varies the depth at all**.

***3. And 0.604 is precisely where every X-Bow assist turns itself off (a). This is the whole story.*** `xbow_forward_board_y` is **0.58**, deliberately tuned so the pro row 0.604-0.609 counts as DEFENSIVE (`test_xbow_live_depth.py:62-66`). The model plays **exclusively** at 0.604. All three assists -- `xbow_target_lane_cell` (reward.py:445), `xbow_lock_cell` (492), `xbow_offense_depth_cell` (539) -- return `None` for `cy >= defense_y`. **Therefore the entire X-Bow assist layer has been inert by construction, for every bow, since the cut was introduced.** Empirical confirmation: `[assist] XBOW lane` appears **0 times across all 19 recorded runs**.

***RETRACTION of my own framing (c).*** I reported these as separate defects -- a lock ignoring aliveness (11c6e2f), a dead-lane rule gated too tightly (L67bz), a pocket assist to switch off (L67by). **They are one defect: the policy emits placements into a region the assist layer defines as out-of-scope.** The assist layer and the policy were tuned against each other, and I kept patching individual assists without once checking whether ANY of them could fire. The measurement that would have caught it -- count how often each assist actually fires -- is a single grep, and I did not run it until tonight.

*Why this makes the owner's complaint inevitable (a).* The model cannot vary its X-Bow lane by board state (0.62-1.97 bits of entropy), and the only components that could vary it for him were all disabled. A dead enemy tower could never change where a bow went. **"It kept putting xbows in the dead left lane" is the exact predicted behaviour of this system**, not an anomaly.

*What changes it.* L67bz's `dead_lane_any_depth` is the first mechanism in the codebase that can move a bow by tower state at 0.604. Unit-tested and now instrumented (`[assist] XBOW dead-lane`), but **NOT verified live** -- one run settles it.

*What this does NOT establish.* Why the policy is degenerate on this one card (untested; likely the imitation data, since pro X-Bows cluster on that row -- but pros VARY the lane by tower state and this model does not). Whether raising the cut would be better than the L67bz fix -- untested, and it would re-enable the run15 bridge-shove regression (16 of 17 bows to the bridge). Anything about live winrate: **still never measured, not once, in this entire project** -- every number given to the owner has been engine ghosts.


**BN. L67cb -- THE LIVE OUTCOME LEDGER: this project has never recorded a single live match result, and now it does. Written under an 8%-usage / 6.5-hour deadline, sequenced so every stopping point leaves a working repo.** Owner 2026-09-18, after an ultimatum and a budget cut to 6.5 hours: *"you have 6.5 hours to measure the baseline. If you cannot do that, spare me the false hope and close it now."*

***The blocking finding (a, verified not assumed).*** **No live match outcome has ever been recorded in this project's history.** `vision.py` has no results-screen reader -- its line 11 ("Reward detection (tower HP / crowns) is added with the RL fine-tune step") is a NOTE, not an implementation. `play.py` logged no outcome. I grepped all 19 `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/live_run*_utf8.log` and every `icebow/data/play_*.log` for `victory|defeat|crowns_for|outcome`: the only hits are the bare word `outcome` (5 in run20, 14 in run18), which are `[ability] FROSTY outcome +7s` hero lines. **An earlier grep of mine appeared to show outcomes existed; that was a false positive and I checked it before reporting.** Consequence: **the owner's "reconstruct the baseline from sessions on disk" is impossible** -- there is nothing to reconstruct, and every winrate ever reported to him came from engine ghosts.

***The change (L67cb, one file, additive).*** `icebow/src/clashrl/play.py`:
- `_ledger` + `_match` counters declared beside `prev`/`last_act` (~:1293).
- `_match["t0"] = time.time()` in the **new-match** branch (~:1327).
- The ledger write in the **match-end** branch, straight after `_replay_rec.end_match()` (~:1334) -- a block that already runs **exactly once per match**.
- Outcome source: `TowerTracker.crown_counts()` (`reward.py:722`) plus **`king_trending_down()` (`reward.py:737`)**. The latter is essential and easy to miss: a king fall ends the match instantly, so its destruction latch frequently cannot finish before the frame cuts to the results screen -- **without it, 3-crown wins are systematically under-read**. Crowns decide a CR match (equal crowns = draw), so no results-screen OCR is needed.
- **Correctness point:** `tower_tracker.reset()` runs at match START, not at end, so the latches still hold THIS match when the hook reads them. Verified in the source, not assumed.
- Writes `icebow/data/live_matches_<session>.jsonl`, one row: `n, t_end, seconds, outcome, crowns_for, crowns_against, king_latched, king_trending, overtime_hint, ckpt, tau`. Plus a `[match] WIN 1-0 182s | session 3W-1L-0D of 4` line to the session log.
- Wrapped in `try/except` -- a ledger line must never kill the live loop (same discipline as L67by). **REVERT: delete the three blocks; nothing else depends on them.**

***Instrument validated BEFORE any live match (a).*** `scratchpad/validate_ledger.py` constructs TowerTracker states and checks the full mapping -- including that `blue`/`red` are not inverted (the failure that would have logged every win as a loss), both king-latched cases, and both king-**trending** recoveries. Reading the docstring was not treated as verification; that habit is what produced this session's retractions.

*What the measurement can and cannot say.* At ~19 matches/h (measured from `play_20260917_233152.log`: 3:02 / 3:03 / 1:59 / 3:04 with ~8 s between), ~5.5 h gives **~105-115 matches, Wilson 95% CI about +-9 points**. That separates 50% from 30%. It does **not** separate 45% from 55%. It also **cannot distinguish real players from bots** -- trophy road serves both and no reader exists, so it measures "winrate vs whatever matchmaking served", which is weaker than the owner's stated bar. No trophy reader exists either; `trophy_hint` was dropped from the schema rather than faked.

*Runbook for a fresh session.* Launch: `--student data\pipeline\s1_icebow_v6aug_s1.pt --student-gate-tau 0.27` (flags already committed: `opp_elixir_v2`/`student_opp_elixir` config.yaml:1291/1297, pocket assist OFF :1371, dead-lane fix ON). Nothing else is to be changed during the run -- it measures what exists today. Then parse `icebow/data/live_matches_*.jsonl` for winrate + Wilson CI, and cross-check that the row count equals the `IN_MATCH` transitions in the session log; a mismatch means matches were dropped and the denominator is wrong. Free extras from the same log, no code needed: plays/min, >10 s pause share, `[assist] XBOW dead-lane` firings, spells cast on unconfirmed detections.

*What this does NOT establish.* Any live winrate -- at the time of writing the run had not been executed. Whether the crown latch is correct at end-of-match **in live conditions** (validated offline against constructed states only; the plan calls for 5 hand-checked matches before trusting a long run). Nothing about RL, velocity, or any other pending work.

**BP. L67cd -- ROOT CAUSE OF BOTH LOST SESSIONS: `WindowCapture` grabs a SCREEN RECTANGLE, so any window on top of the game is what the bot "sees". Check this before every live run.** Diagnosed 2026-09-18 17:53 after the owner reported the bot "can't even find the battle button".

***The mechanism (a).*** `icebow/src/clashrl/capture.py:43-61` `refresh_region()` resolves the game window's client area to a rectangle `[left, top, width, height]` in physical screen pixels, and `grab()` then captures **that region of the screen** via mss -- not the window's own pixels. **Anything drawn over that rectangle is captured verbatim and fed to the detector as if it were the game.**

***What it actually captured (a).*** `run.py diag` -> `icebow/data/diag_state.png` shows **a browser window displaying the Claude Code conversation**, not Clash Royale. Consequences, all consistent: `detect_state -> UNKNOWN` on every frame (it is a web page); match_end templates score 0.303/0.317 against a 0.80 threshold; the reported "Battle button best-match center = (0.570, 0.866)" is a **spurious template hit on page content**, well away from the configured tap `[0.492, 0.771]`; and nav's escalations -- reward tap `(0.500, 0.550)` and dismiss `(0.645, 0.905)` -- were **synthesising mouse clicks onto the browser** for minutes. The owner's "can't find the battle button" was the bot not looking at the game at all.

***This is the same failure as the antivirus episode (a).*** The "Antivirus protection expired" dialog (BO) that killed 22 relaunch attempts overnight was another window over the same rectangle. **Two lost sessions, one root cause.** It is not a nav bug, a template bug, or a model bug.

*Config is NOT the problem.* `window.title_contains: "Clash Royale"`, `window.region: null` (config.yaml:9-10), so the region auto-detects by title on every refresh. Note the trap for later: if `window.region` is ever pinned, `refresh_region()` short-circuits at `capture.py:44` (`self._explicit`) and a stale rectangle can never self-correct.

*Not fixable from inside the process (a).* `SetForegroundWindow` + `ShowWindow` on the game's own handle were tried and failed -- Windows blocks foreground-stealing from a background process, which is also why `nav`'s force-focus fails. Synthetic input to rearrange windows was declined on judgement (the occluding window showed a purchase control) and, for the security dialog, blocked by the permission classifier.

***THE PRE-FLIGHT CHECK, and it would have saved both sessions.*** Before launching, run `python run.py diag` and confirm the saved `data/diag_state.png` shows **the actual game**. `[diag] detect_state -> UNKNOWN` at the Home screen means the capture is hijacked -- do not launch. The game window must be on top and unobstructed for the whole run; a bot that cannot see the game cannot play, and it will click blindly wherever its escalations aim.

*Matches banked so far (not a winrate).* 11 total across two sessions, same ckpt/tau (`s1_icebow_v6aug_s1.pt`, 0.27): 9 from 01:13-01:40 (3W-6L) and 2 from 17:35-17:42 (1W-1L, both to overtime). `score_live_baseline.py` pools them and reports per-file counts.

*What this does NOT establish.* Any live winrate. Whether the game screen is otherwise healthy -- the only capture on disk is of the browser, so nothing here says the Home screen would be detected correctly once unobstructed.


**BQ. L67ce -- THE BOT PLAYS NOTHING, SILENTLY, IF THE IN-GAME DECK DOES NOT MATCH THE CONFIGURED DECK -- and an `IN_MATCH`-based health check does not catch it.** Diagnosed 2026-09-18 18:08 after a run produced five "matches" in seven minutes with impossible scorelines.

***The symptom (a).*** Five ledger rows in ~7 minutes, durations **51 / 38 / 128 / 85 / 63 s**, outcomes `LOSS 0-1`, `LOSS 0-1`, `LOSS 0-1`, `LOSS 0-2`, `LOSS 0-1`. None of those end a Clash Royale match -- one tower down does not end a game, and 38 s cannot three-crown from full HP. Decisive counter: **`taps=0`, `waits=0` across all five**, where five real matches should produce hundreds of decisions.

***The cause (a).*** `run.py diag` -> `data/diag_state.png` shows a **real match in progress** (1:30 left, opponent "ENZO PRO" at 10000 trophies, enemy push mid-board) -- but the tap hand holds **Fireball (4), a 1-cost, a 6-cost and a 3-cost**, none of them icebow cards. The account's active deck was not the configured deck. `recognize_hand` therefore matches nothing, `act_in_match` early-returns before the student ever decides (`play.py:801`), and the bot stands still while a real opponent dismantles it.

***The configured deck (a), from `load_deck('icebow').cards` -- the same loader the student uses:*** `tornado, tesla_evo, ice_wizard, x_bow, rocket, knight_evo, the_log, skeletons`. **Two are EVOLUTIONS** -- Evolution Tesla and Evolution Knight. Plain Tesla or plain Knight will not match the templates.

***The verification trap, and I walked straight into it.*** My 6-minute health check asserted `IN_MATCH > 0` and printed **"PLAYING OK"**. `IN_MATCH` was genuinely fine -- the bot *was* in matches. **The health check must assert `taps > 0`, not `IN_MATCH > 0`.** A deck mismatch produces a perfectly healthy-looking state machine driving a policy that never acts.

*A correction I owe the record.* I first called these five rows "fabricated". **They are not.** They are **real match losses** -- the bot genuinely lost, because it played nothing. They are invalid as a measurement of the *policy* (it never acted), not invalid as match outcomes. Quarantined to `live_matches_20260918_180120.jsonl.INVALID` so they cannot pool into the winrate; the reasoning in the first commit message was wrong even though the action was right.

*Valid data unaffected.* 11 rows remain across two sessions at `s1_icebow_v6aug_s1.pt` / tau 0.27 -- 9 from 01:13-01:40 and 2 from 17:35-17:42. Run 1 logged 261 taps of `skeletons`, `the_log`, `tornado`, `x_bow`, `tesla`, confirming it was genuinely on-deck.

***PRE-FLIGHT, now two checks, both cheap.*** (1) `python run.py diag` and **look** at `data/diag_state.png` -- confirm it shows the real game, not another window (BP). (2) After launch, confirm **`taps > 0`** within the first few minutes -- `IN_MATCH > 0` is not sufficient. Either check alone would have saved a session; together they cover both known silent-failure modes.

*What this does NOT establish.* Why the active deck changed between 17:42 and 18:01. Whether the deck can be verified programmatically before launch -- `vision.deck_keys` vs the tray read would be the obvious check and is **not implemented**; `play.py:365-369` warns on a checkpoint/deck mismatch but not on a *tray* mismatch.


**BR. L67cf -- RETRACTION: I KILLED A HEALTHY RUN. My abort check grepped a file that never contains the lines it counted, so it was structurally guaranteed to fire. The owner was right; the bot was playing correctly.** 2026-09-18 18:31.

***The error (a).*** The 3-minute abort check counted `[student] TAP` and `[student] WAIT` in `icebow/data/play_<ts>.log`. **Those lines are printed directly to stdout and never routed through `log()`, so they never appear in that file.** Control, decisive: the known-good 17:35 session played **2 complete matches** and its session log contains **0 TAP lines in 20 total lines**. The check therefore reads zero regardless of how well the policy is playing. It could never have passed.

***What the run was actually doing (a).*** From the stdout capture `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/live_baseline_20260918_182802.log` (20,552 bytes): **26 TAPs, 21 WAITs**, cards `tesla_evo`, `skeletons`, `knight`, `x_bow`, `tornado`, `ice_wizard` -- **exactly the configured icebow deck**. The final tap is timestamped **18:31:15.008**; the abort killed the process at **18:31:15**. The run was mid-match and playing correctly when it was destroyed.

***Correcting the previous record.*** Commit `f8b3cdf` (§BQ) states the 18:28 run aborted on a deck mismatch. **That is wrong.** The deck was correct by then -- the owner had fixed it after the genuine 18:08 mismatch, which was independently evidenced by the diag screenshot showing Fireball and other non-icebow cards. §BQ's *18:08* diagnosis stands on that screenshot; its implication that the 18:28 abort proved a continuing mismatch does not.

***The compounding failure, which is the real lesson.*** §BQ's stated remedy was "the health check must assert `taps > 0`, not `IN_MATCH > 0`." That remedy was implemented against the wrong data source, so it converted a *detection* problem into a *false-positive* problem -- and then I trusted the broken instrument over the owner's direct report that the deck was correct. **A check that has never been observed to pass is not a check; it is an unvalidated assumption with an if-statement around it.** The control that exposed it (grep a known-good log for the same pattern) takes one command and should have been run before the check was ever armed.

*Data status.* Valid ledger unchanged at **11 rows** (9 + 2), 4W-7L. The 18:28 run wrote **no** row -- killed before `MATCH_END`. The 5 rows quarantined as `live_matches_20260918_180120.jsonl.INVALID` remain quarantined: the 18:08 screenshot is independent evidence that those matches really were played on the wrong deck, though note that my *taps=0* reasoning for them came from the same broken grep and is not itself evidence.

*Correct instrumentation for any future check.* Count plays from the **stdout capture** (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/live_baseline_*.log`), not from `icebow/data/play_*.log`. The session log carries only `log()` output -- state transitions, nav lines, `[match]` rows. `[student] TAP`/`WAIT`, `[assist]` and the per-decision telemetry exist only on stdout.

*What this does NOT establish.* Whether the policy plays *well* -- 26 taps in one partial match says the pipeline works, nothing about quality. No live winrate; still never measured. Whether any earlier conclusion in this session rested on the same wrong-file grep beyond the two identified here.


**BS. L67cg -- THE FIRST LIVE WINRATE EVER MEASURED IN THIS PROJECT: 35.1% over 37 matches (95% CI 21.8-51.2%). The owner's bar of 50% is not reached, and the engine-to-live transfer gap is now measured rather than asserted.** 2026-09-18, two sessions run by the owner (19:08, 19:41) pooled with two earlier ones, all on `s1_icebow_v6aug_s1.pt` at tau 0.27.

***The number (a).*** **37 matches, 13W-22L-2D = 35.1%, Wilson 95% CI [21.8%, 51.2%].** Excluding the single 0-0 finish this instrument cannot resolve: 36.1% (CI 22.5-52.4%). Median match 183 s, 2.02 h of play, crowns **23 for / 40 against**.

| session | n | record | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 011324 | 9 | 3W-6L | 33.3% |
| 173530 | 2 | 1W-1L | (too small) |
| 190851 (owner) | 8 | 3W-5L | 37.5% |
| 194128 (owner) | 18 | 6W-10L-2D | 33.3% |

**No single session drives the result** -- the three meaningful ones land at 33.3 / 37.5 / 33.3. There is no heterogeneity to explain away, which is the precondition for trusting a pooled figure.

***Against the owner's bar: NOT reached (a).*** The interval's upper edge touches 51.2%, so 50% is not formally excluded at n=37 -- but the point estimate is 35% and three independent sessions concentrate there. Reading the CI edge against the weight of the data would be reporting the number one wants.

***The engine-to-live gap, measured for the first time (a).*** This same checkpoint at this same tau scored **74% against engine ghosts** (§BI / `score_attrib_e2_v6aug_s1_tau027`). Live: **35.1%**. A **~39-point gap.** The engine figure is separately known to be inflated by a measured artifact: 29% of engine matches outlive the scripted opponent and 27 of those 29 are wins (§BM). This is the quantitative form of the owner's standing objection that engine numbers do not translate.

***The sharpest behavioural finding (a).*** **21 of the owner's 26 matches went to overtime (81%).** Overtime means neither side destroyed a tower in three full minutes of regulation. With crowns 23 for / 40 against and a median match of 183 s, the profile is a bot that **defends competently and almost never closes**. That is far more specific than "it plays badly", and it points at the win condition -- consistent with the X-Bow placement entropy of 0.62-1.97 bits measured in §BM, where the deck's win condition is the one degenerate card.

*Instrument validation (a).* **Integrity verified per session, not assumed:** 190851 = 8 rows / 8 `IN_MATCH` / 8 `[match]`; 194128 = 18 rows / 19 `IN_MATCH`, the 19th match being cut off mid-play when the owner stopped the run (last log line `20:43:59 state: IN_MATCH`, process gone by 20:47). **3 of 37 matches were 3-crown finishes recovered by `king_trending_down`** -- without it they would have scored 1-0 or 2-0 instead of 0-3.

*How these rows were distinguished from the invalid ones (a).* Ten rows from the 18:01 and 18:40 runs are quarantined as `.INVALID` (bot in matches but never playing). The discriminator, established empirically: zero-play matches ran **38-128 s ending 0-1/0-2 with `crowns_for` pinned at 0 and no draws**; these sessions have **median 190 s / 183 s, `crowns_for` reaching 1 and 2, and 2 draws**. One short match in each session, not a pattern.

***What is NOT available, and it matters (b).*** **No behaviour counters for the owner's sessions** -- plays/min, >10 s pause share, `[assist] XBOW dead-lane` firings, rocket usage. Those print only to stdout and the sessions were run without redirect. **So this 35% cannot be connected to any of the owner's four behaviour complaints.** Fix for next time is one shell token: `> run.log 2>&1`. Note also that `score_live_baseline.py` will silently compute its integrity check and behaviour counters from whatever `live_baseline_*.log` files exist -- i.e. from OTHER sessions -- so only its winrate block is trustworthy when a session was run without redirect.

*What this does NOT establish.* Whether 35% is the ceiling of this checkpoint or of this pipeline. Whether the trophy band shifted during collection (no trophy reader exists, so the winrate is not binned by opponent strength and ladder matchmaking pushes every player toward 50% over time). Anything about RL, velocity, or the gate. To settle the 50% bar needs ~200 matches for +-7 pp -- about 12 h at the ~17 matches/h these sessions achieved.

### §5cs.98 -- L67e+f (2026-09-08 06:00-18:00 UTC): **OPTION B GRADED (3 seeds: clean 21.56 +- 0.07, degraded 19.45 +- 0.05) BUT ITS GAIN IS AGAINST A CORRUPTION MODEL WE NOW KNOW IS WRONG. Three label-free live measurements instead: the GATE survives real detector input (live .248-.325 vs engine .294-.298), PLACEMENT COLLAPSES toward the prior (top-1 cell share 0.25 vs 0.07 at matched unit counts), and nothing JITTERS (same-cell 61.4% live vs 38.7% engine -- the collapse seen twice, not a second defect). Ablation names the cause: MISSING VALUES (unit HP, exact/opponent elixir, king HP), not noisy ones -- spell tokens, unknown team tags and low confidence each do NOTHING. Against pro labels, SUPPLYING beats FLAGGING (blank_both 18.78 exact cell / 52.11 card -> fill_both 20.15 / 63.25), so the fill is now wired live and verified (live top-1 share 0.411 -> 0.322)**

**A. Option B, the 3-seed result (a), `s1_v6aug/eval_v3val_icebow_v6aug.out` + `eval_v3degraded_*`.** Augmented set = 622,923 rows (339,192 clean + 283,731 degraded TRAIN rows; val rows clean, so checkpoint selection is v6lat's own rule).

| metric | v6lat | v6aug | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| exact cell, clean v3 VAL | 21.04 +- 0.22 | **21.56 +- 0.07** | +0.52 |
| exact cell, degraded VAL | 16.35 +- 0.56 | **19.45 +- 0.05** | +3.10 |
| card top-1, degraded | 49.3 +- 1.2 | **60.4 +- 0.6** | +11.1 |

Caveats (both material): seed 0 is a **13-epoch crashed run** (CUDA error under two trainers + the detector on one 8 GB GPU), so it is best-of-13, not best-of-20; and the degraded-VAL gain is **partly circular** -- trained on `degrade()`, graded on `degrade()`. Live, both v6aug seeds are near-catatonic at the training threshold (play rate 0.7-1.3% vs v6lat's 15% on the same 300 frames) -- NOT a broken gate but a shifted one: the tau reproducing v6lat's live rate is 0.16 (s0) / 0.083 (s1), not 0.5. **RETRACTION of the L67e chat claim that the augmented arm "loses on the thing we care about": it is a calibration difference, and its live placement quality is unmeasured.**

**B. Placement collapses live; the gate does not (a).** Same model, same rule, two input pipelines, matched on information content (>= 3 units, elixir >= 5) and on sample size (n=159 both sides):

| top-1 cell share | engine v3 VAL | real live frames |
|---|---|---|
| all rows | 0.07-0.11 | 0.25 (matched) / 0.40-0.62 (raw, per session) |
| units 2-3 | **0.10** | **0.33** |
| units 4-6 | **0.07** | **0.24** |
| units 0-1 | 0.33 | 0.53 |

Both halves matter: **sparsity alone collapses the head** (engine at 0-1 units is 0.33, and live frames carry a median of 2-3 units), *and* at matched sparsity live is still ~3x more concentrated. Detector recall would fix the first half only. The cells live collapses onto (1267, 1289 = lattice row 35, cols 7 and 29) are the model's own #2/#3 engine cells, so this is a fallback to its prior, not a coordinate bug -- the mirrored x-medians across sessions (0.194 / 0.806) were the first suspicion and are explained by the two mirrored favourites, not by a warp fault.

**C. No jitter (a), `place_stability.py`, decision gaps matched (live pairs 1.0 s, engine 0.5-2.5 s).** Same-cell fraction live **61.4%** vs engine **38.7%**; median move when it changes 6.00 vs 6.04 tiles, p90 13.1 vs 13.9, moves > 5 tiles 53.7% vs 57.7%. Detector noise is NOT shaking the placement head -- live is *more* repetitive, which is B's collapse seen through a second instrument and must not be reported as an independent finding. Note the 6-tile median move is large on BOTH sides: a property of the model, not of the live path, so it belongs to the pro-agreement problem.

**D. What causes the collapse (a), `ablate_live.py` -- one detector pass over 300 live frames, every variant re-scored on the same cached BoardStates.**

| live input variant | top-1 share | distinct |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 0.400 | 43 |
| spell tokens removed | 0.417 | 39 |
| `side=-1` resolved | 0.390 | 42 |
| `conf` forced to 1.0 | 0.403 | 41 |
| **unit HP supplied** | **0.303** | 57 |
| **scalars supplied** (exact elixir, opp elixir, king HP) | **0.287** | 46 |
| all of the above | **0.243** | 54 |

**CONTRADICTED (c): the spell-token hypothesis.** §5cs.95 A and §5cs.97 both flagged the 29-78 live spell tokens per run (training rows contain zero) as a likely cause; removing them makes concentration marginally WORSE (0.417 vs 0.400). Same for `side=-1` (training: zero unknown sides) and for detector confidence. The head is not confused by unfamiliar or noisy values -- it degrades on **absent** ones. Residual after supplying everything is 0.243, still ~2x the matched engine baseline, so missing values are a large part but NOT all of it (b: the unit-count-matched version of the "all" variant is the next measurement).

**E. Supplying beats flagging, measured against PRO LABELS (a), `fill_vs_blank.py`, v3 VAL, v6lat_s0.** Dispersion is label-free, and filling a missing field with a plausible constant is a lie that could disperse the output while making it worse -- so the same manipulation was run where the labels are pro placements:

| input | exact cell | card top-1 | mean dist | gate acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| clean | 20.97 | 65.46 | 3.513 | .826 |
| blank HP / fill HP | 19.47 / **20.26** | 58.77 / **64.01** | 3.991 / **3.652** | .799 / .813 |

Fill beats blank on every metric. Also: **blank_both (18.78) is the closest labelled analogue of today's live input and sits 2.19 pp below clean, not the 4.2 pp `degrade()` predicted** -- the third independent sign (after the gate distribution and the live play rate) that the corruption model overstates the live penalty.

**F. Wired and verified (a).** `obs_contract.LiveReads` gains `opp_elixir` (default None, so training is untouched) and `from_live` gains `unit_hp_default`; `student_live.live_reads` sends the king's alive-proxy HP instead of None; `play.py` hands over the `OpponentElixirEstimator` reading it already computes and was discarding. ### §5cs.97 -- L67d (2026-09-07 22:00-02:30 UTC): **THE STUDENT IS WIRED TO THE LIVE PATH (off by default) AND HAS NOW SEEN REAL DETECTOR OUTPUT. First measurement from it contradicts a premise of S4: with elixir matched, the play gate on REAL live frames tracks the ENGINE (frac p>0.5: live 24.8-32.5% across 3 seeds x 3 sessions vs engine 29.4-29.8%), while `degrade()` -- the model of the live shift that the whole -4.2 pp finding rests on -- inflates it to 44.6-52.4%. The modelled shift is not the real one on this axis, and the degraded VAL is NOT a proxy for live gating. Latency measured: student 28.7-37.6 ms per decision, detector 45-80 ms**

**A. The wiring (a), `icebow/src/clashrl/student_live.py` (new, 175 lines) + `play.py` (+41 lines).** `LiveReads` is assembled from play.py's own readers (`vision.read_elixir`, `recognize_hand`, the single `recognize_next` read, `TowerHpTracker`, `TowerTracker`, `ElixirClock`), in the CONTRACT's tower order (my K,L,R then opp K,L,R -- not play.py's `_tower_frac` order (L,R,king)), with king hp None (`hp_known=0`, it is never printed on screen). Then `from_live` -> `to_tokens` -> `S1Model`, encoding ONCE and reading the card-conditioned cell head off the same encoding. Two mappings the survey (§5cs.95 A) flagged as missing are implemented: **deck slot -> tray id on the BASE key** (the student has 8 base slots, live has 10 identities because an evolved slot carries a second `<key>_evo` identity, so `tesla`/`tesla_evo` both resolve to slot 1 and the tap uses whichever the tray shows), and **cell 2304 (36x64 lattice) -> board (`cell_xy`, off=0.0) -> `warp.board_to_frame` -> `actions.cell_at`** (the 18x24 live grid; L62i measured that quantisation adds 0.000 tiles for in-reach x-bows). `past` is fed from accepted taps.

Live behaviour is UNCHANGED unless `play.student_ckpt` is set (measured: the key resolves to None on the current config, and the added block is skipped). When set, the student decides (card, cell) ONLY -- `deploy_clamp`, the aim assists, the affordability mask and the tap path all still run on its answer -- and an unaffordable or unmappable answer is a **WAIT**, never a silent fall-back to the CNN (mixing two policies inside one match would make any live reading uninterpretable). Revert = unset `play.student_ckpt`, or `git revert 597ddb7`.

**B. Dry run on real frames (a), `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/student_dryrun.py`.** Real recorded sessions, the real YOLO detector at the live `observation.detector_conf`, no game and no clicks: 5 runs over 3 sessions x 3 seeds, 223-400 frames each. Student decision **28.7-37.6 ms median** (p95 61 ms), detector 45-80 ms -> ~75-115 ms per decision against an `act_period` of 1.5 s, so latency is not a constraint (a). Play rate at tau 0.5: 12.6-19.5%; 4-9 distinct cards and 8-19 distinct cells chosen (it is not stuck on one answer); `no_mappable_card` 5-9% of frames (the tray read failed). **Spell tokens appear live (29-78 per run) and the training rows contain ZERO** (§5cs.95 A) -- an unseen token type on every live frame that carries a spell.

**C. The finding (a): `degrade()` mis-models the live shift on the gate axis.** `gate_dist.py`, one model, one rule, three input sources, **elixir >= 5 on both sides** (the uncontrolled first read -- engine 24.7% / live 17.2% / degraded 37.3% -- was confounded by the elixir mix of a uniform frame sample and is superseded within this loop):

| frac p_play > 0.5 | engine v3 VAL (n=9,620) | degrade() twin (same rows) | real live frames (n=116-257) |
|---|---|---|---|
| v6lat s0, session 20260815 | .296 | .446 | **.303** |
| v6lat s0, session 20260804_173304 | .296 | .446 | **.267** |
| v6lat s1, session 20260815 | .298 | .511 | **.325** |
| v6lat s2, session 20260815 | .294 | .524 | **.248** |

Real live sits ON the engine number (24.8-32.5% vs 29.4-29.8%); the modelled shift pushes the gate 15-23 pp HIGHER, i.e. it makes the student trigger-happy in a way the real detector does not. Replicated on 3 seeds and on a session the first read never touched.

What this does NOT establish (b): that `degrade()` is wrong about PLACEMENT or CARD choice -- those have no live ground truth here, and the -4.2 pp / -12.4 pp of §5cs.95 A remain the only numbers on that axis (they are measured on the twin, and what this loop shows is that the twin is not a faithful stand-in for live at least where the gate is concerned). Confounds that remain: live frames are NOT paired with VAL rows (only elixir is matched -- board occupancy, match phase and cycle position still differ); live n is 116-257 after the filter against 9,620 engine rows; the sessions are the owner's own recordings from 2026-08-04/15 replayed through today's detector.

**D. What it changes.** (1) The S4 premise "the live student will be much worse than the bench student" is weaker than §5cs.95 stated: on the one axis now measurable live, real input costs nothing. (2) Option B (running) trains against `degrade()`; a gain on the degraded VAL therefore is NOT evidence of a live gain, and B's report must say so. (3) The cheapest way to settle placement is the same trick as the gate: the owner's recorded sessions have HIS clicks (`events.jsonl`), so a `from_live` state at each own-click gives a live-labelled placement set -- the L63 own-click test already built exactly this and can be re-pointed at the student (next loop).

**E. Two of my own bugs, both caught by the box.** (i) `merge_aug.py` indexed an `NpzFile` inside a loop -- `d["tok"][a:b]` decompresses the WHOLE 74 MB array on every access, so 283,731 rows meant 283,731 decompressions and a `MemoryError`; fixed by materialising both token arrays once and gathering with a vectorised ragged range. (ii) Three `train_s1` processes in parallel drove free RAM from 4.7 GB to **160 MB** (2.3 GB each) -- seeds 1 and 2 were killed at epoch 0 (nothing lost) and the guardrail "check free RAM and CPU before launching" is now also true of parallel seeds: TWO fit on this box, three do not.

**F. State.** Option B running: seeds 0+1 in parallel on the 622,923-row augmented set (339,192 clean + 283,731 degraded TRAIN rows; val rows stay clean so checkpoint selection is v6lat's own rule), ~16 min/epoch, 20 epochs -> seeds 0+1 land ~07:00-08:30 UTC, then a 2-seed SCREEN on both VALs while seed 2 trains (lands ~13:00 UTC). Three-seed result is the one that counts; the 2-seed read is labelled a screen. Box: 2 trainers, 4.0 GB free. Not committed: parquet, corpora, npz, dry-run jsonl.

### §5cs.96 -- L67c (2026-09-07 18:00-22:33 UTC): **OPTION A RUN AND THE HEADLINE IS A NULL: 603 extra replays mined out of FirstLight's public 252k dataset (+0.45 corpus doublings) moved exact cell 20.93 -> 21.04 (+0.11 pp, band +-0.5) against a pre-registered +0.7 pp -- the S2 scaling line does NOT extend to this foreign corpus. **A. Two retractions first.** §5cs.95 C claimed "~2,070 exact-icebow sides" in `VanguardX101/IL_Replay` from shard 0 (41 per 5,000 = 0.41%). **B. The pipeline (a).** All 52 replay parts downloaded (825 MB, sha256 52/52 ok). `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/hf_to_crawl.py` converts HF `payload_json` events to crawl2 `battles.csv`/`plays_ext.csv` (team=blue=data_s "t", raw RoyaleAPI x/y, `attr_i` preserved so the loader's own 180-degree rotation applies, abilities kept as `attr_ability=1`/`_invalid` so the play count matches). Driven through both local engine slots (37031/37032, `--record-every 20 --record-plays --level 11`, the v3/v5 recipe): **603 converted, 163 failed, every failure the same known sandbox gap -- `ValueError: card has no native evolution form: 26000043`** (already parked in §6). **C. The number (a), `scratchpad/gauntlet/L67/s1_v6/eval_v3val_icebow_v6lat.out`, 3 seeds, same 13,761-row / 3,796-play v3 VAL as 18.17 / 19.84 / 20.93.**

The card move is 1.96 pp against seed spreads of 0.28 and 0.57 -- ~4 sd, and NLL and placement error move the same way, so it is not a single-metric wobble.

**D. What this establishes, and what it does not.** Established (a): **the S2 slope (+1.6 pp/doubling, measured on OUR crawl across v3/v4/v5) does not transfer to this corpus** -- the same instrument, the same deck, one change (603 more replays), no cell gain. Established (a): the same data DOES improve card choice and calibration, so the replays are not junk and the conversion is not broken (a broken conversion would degrade both heads, not improve one). NOT established (b): *why* the two heads split. Three candidates, none tested: (i) skill/tier -- these are Ranked max-level games, not the pro/ladder-top tier our crawl targets, and placement is the tier-sensitive skill while card choice is more deck-determined; (ii) the placement head is at a *representation* ceiling, not a data ceiling (consistent with §5cs.48 phase-not-resolution and §5cs.94's saturating rollout, both of which said the objective/inputs, not the sample count, are what bind); (iii) engine-drive noise on foreign replays (78.4% crowns match) adds label noise that hurts the spatially precise head more than the categorical one. The cheapest discriminator for (i) vs (ii) is a **held-out split by source**: score v6lat separately on the HF-sourced val rows and the crawl-sourced val rows -- if placement agreement is lower on HF rows specifically, it is tier; if equal, it is the head.

**F. The B decision (the owner's ruling was "A first, then make a decision after on whether B should be done or not"). DECISION: DO B.** Reasons from this loop's numbers: (1) A closed the data axis for placement -- the lever that was supposed to be worth +0.7 pp returned +0.11 pp, so buying more clean replays is no longer the best use of a 4-hour block; (2) E shows the live shift is untouched by A, and the shift (-4.2 pp cell, -12.4 pp card) is still the single largest measured loss between the bench student and anything that would run on screen; (3) B is the last cheap thing on the S4 path -- no new data collection, 3 seeds on the dataset we now have. Design, one change: train on **corpus v6** (the base is held fixed at v6 for both arms so "augmentation" is the only variable) with `obs_contract.degrade` applied as training augmentation, 3 seeds, graded on the unchanged clean v3 VAL AND the degraded twin. Pre-registration: the honest hope is recovering a chunk of the -4.2 pp on the degraded VAL; the risk to watch is the clean VAL falling (augmentation trading bench accuracy for robustness), and BOTH numbers get reported whichever way they go.

**G. State.** Box: 3 python (2 unrelated services + the chain); v6lat s0/s1/s2 at `icebow/data/pipeline/s1_icebow_v6lat_s{0,1,2}.pt`, dataset at `s1_dataset_v6.npz` (local only, not committed).
