### §5cs.70 -- L64k (2026-09-06 11:1x-12:0x UTC): **the S1 placement label is quantised with `floor` on a grid whose cell BOUNDARIES are the pro placement lattice, so a 1-unit crawl jitter (the same lattice point is served as `500k` in some replays and `500k-1` in others) flips the label one cell at random. In v3 hogeq 126 of the 455 physical lattice points carry two different half-tile labels and 71.8% of play rows sit on the jittered side; the rotation of the i=1 half (18000-x) flips which side the jitter lands, so the naive v4 corpus mixes both -- its first checkpoint reads tile top-1 0.2328 vs 0.2130 but exact-cell 0.1365 vs 0.2003 and NLL 4.18 vs 3.90. The engine inverse (`cell_center`, +0.5 cell) also placed every model card 250 units (0.25 tile) off the lattice. Fix = one convention change, `--grid lattice` (round; lattice points are cell centres; inverse lands ON the lattice), default `floor` untouched so every v3 checkpoint reads exactly as before.**

**A. The trap, measured (a), `L64/s1_v4/lattice_phase_hogeq.txt`, `lattice_type_by_pos.txt`, `boundary_rows.txt`, `grid_verify.txt`.** Every crawl x/y is `500k` or `500k-1` units (x%500 in {0, 499}; y likewise) -- the pro placement lattice is the half-tile lattice, tile centres at odd k. At the SAME point both spellings occur (x=500: 152 at 500 vs 720 at 499; y=17500: 848 vs 3,875), so the `-1` carries no placement information (0.001 tile). `model_v3.cell_index` floors x*36, and 500k/18000*36 = k exactly: the lattice point IS the cell boundary, so `500k-1` -> cell k-1 and `500k` -> cell k. In the v3 hogeq npz 100% of play labels sit within 0.02 cell of a boundary; after the side-1 mirror (all hogeq rows are side 1) x is consistent but y is not: 71.8% of rows at frac 0.98+, 28.2% at 0 -> **126 of 455 lattice points have two floor labels**. Rotating the i=1 half (x' = 18000-x) turns `500k-1` into `500m+1`, which floors to the nominal cell: the two halves of corpus_v4 disagree on x too (v4 npz: x 37.1% jittered vs v3 22.1%).
**B. What it did to the naive v4 run (a, one seed, v3 val 6,133 rows, `eval_preview_s0.out`).** v4 s0 (63,769 rows, 463 replays, play share 29.4% vs v3 29.5%): tile top-1 **0.2328** vs v3 s0 0.2130, card 0.583 vs 0.547, gate bal-acc 0.688 vs 0.627, value 0.572 vs 0.549 -- and **cell_half 0.1365 vs 0.2003, cell NLL 4.184 vs 3.899**. More data helps every head except the one whose labels the mix scrambled. (b) Whether the tile-level gain survives a consistent convention is exactly what C's runs measure; do not quote 0.2328 as a data-scaling result.
**C. Fix (a, offline-verified), `pipeline/model_v3.py` (`cell_label`, `tile_of_cell`, `cell_xy`), `train_s1.py --grid {floor,lattice}` (stored in the checkpoint args), `eval_s1.py` and `engine_play.py` read the checkpoint's `grid`.** `lattice` = round(x*36): the +-1-unit jitter cannot flip it, 0 of 455 points get two labels, the round-trip cell -> board -> engine units reproduces the snapped lattice point to 0.000 units on all sampled rows, and `cell_xy(.., "lattice")` puts the engine placement ON the lattice where `floor`'s centre was always 250 units off. Tile labels on v3 are unchanged under the new convention (0.000 of rows differ), so v3 tile numbers stay comparable; exact-cell numbers do NOT (the label set changed for 71.8% of rows) -- compare lattice checkpoints with lattice checkpoints. Regression: `s1_hogeq_s0` still reads 0.2130 / 0.2003 / 3.899 through the patched `eval_s1`; `engine_play` imports; board-blind baseline identical under both (0.1145). Not tested on the engine yet (a lattice checkpoint has to exist first).
**D. Running.** Naive v4 x3 continues to completion as the record of the trap (s1 at epoch 16 at 11:52). Chained after its `HOGEQ_V4_DONE`: hogeq v3 `--grid lattice` x3 (`--tag lat`, the baseline under the new convention) -> eval on v3 val -> hogeq v4 lattice x3 (`--tag v4lat`) -> eval; `s1_v4/run_hogeq_lat.out`, ETA ~14:00 UTC. Icebow i=1 chain armed on its re-fetch (403/615 at 11:43): tags -> drive with v3 flags on 37031 -> fidelity + handedness; the hogeq 24-tag re-fetch resume runs alongside.
What this does NOT establish: the size of the label-noise ceiling (C's v3-lattice band vs 20.99 +/- 0.36 measures it on tile, and cell_half under lattice is a new number with no prior); whether the engine result moves when placements land on the lattice (needs a lattice checkpoint under `--gate sample` vs 85/79/84); anything about icebow (same code path, same lattice: `boundary_rows.txt` icebow v3 x 29.8% / y 39.0% jittered, so the same ceiling applies).
**TRAPS (a):** (1) A label grid whose boundaries coincide with the data's lattice is a coin flip on every boundary point; check the fractional part of x*G before choosing floor. (2) "More data made tile better and cell worse" is a label-convention smell, not a scaling result. (3) `git show HEAD:file | file -` reports LF for files the working copy holds as CRLF (autocrlf): patch scripts must match the working copy's line endings, and mixed endings after a patch are the sign it half-applied.
**E. Next.** Read the v3-lattice band (tile vs 20.99 +/- 0.36; cell_half is a new instrument) and then v4-lattice vs v3-lattice -- the first clean data-scaling point. Then one lattice checkpoint on the hogeq engine instrument (`--gate sample`, same 100 entries) vs 85/79/84.

### §5cs.69 -- L64j (2026-09-06 09:4x-11:1x UTC): **the hogeq engine band CLOSES under the sampled gate -- 85 / 79 / 84 (sd 3.2) vs 53 / 19 / 44 under threshold tau 0.5 (sd 17.6); a random policy matched to the same play volume loses 15-85, so the 83 is the model, not the volume. §5cs.68's "s1 is the outlier" is RETRACTED as a statement about the checkpoint: it was the tau rule. The re-fetched hogeq i=1 half passes fidelity on the full set (winner agreement 65.3% vs 67.2%, y-frame offset 0.008 tiles), the crawler source fix is applied and verified, and one trap cost a re-drive: the chained i=1 drive ran without `--record-every 20`, so its replays had no wait frames.**

**A. Sample-gate band (a), `L64/engine_hogeq/smp_ck{0,1,2}`, scores `score_smp_ck*.txt`, per-decision diffs `ckpt_diff_smp*.txt`; same 100 paired entries, seed 0, `--gate sample` (play iff u < p_gate each 0.5-s decision).** s0 **85-15** (164.3 s, +57.0 +/- 7.7, survived longer 79, crowns against 0.82), s1 **79-21** (145.9 s, +38.6 +/- 6.8, survived longer 75, crowns against 0.97), s2 **84-16** (158.4 s, +51.0 +/- 6.9, survived longer 79, crowns against 0.95). Accepted plays per match 32.9 / 27.4 / 30.5 (threshold: 26.8 / 17.4 / 24.9); offered 20.1-20.7 plays/min with 55-58% accepted (the rest refused for elixir: mean elixir at decision 3.4 vs 8.0-8.7 under threshold -- the sampled policy spends everything it has); first play at 7 s (threshold: 23 s); p_gate p50 falls to 0.14-0.15 (the gate is state-dependent: an empty elixir bar reads as "wait", which is the right answer). Matches are SHORTER than under threshold (146-164 s vs 175-190) because the model 3-crowns (d_crowns_for +2.4 for s1).
**B. The control that makes A a finding (a), `rnd18_s0`, `score_rnd18.txt`.** Random policy at p 0.18 per decision, chosen to match the sample rule's volume: offered 21.1 plays/min, 48.7% accepted, **25.0 accepted plays/match** (sample band: 27-33) -> **15-85**, +38.9 +/- 5.0 s, survived longer 93, crowns against 2.45. The rate-matched random survives as long as s1 does (both +39 s) but wins 15 vs 79-85: at equal volume the difference is what is played and where. (Both randoms, p 0.13 and 0.18, land at 15-18; volume alone buys nothing above no-plays' 0.)
**C. Retraction and the instrument ruling.** §5cs.68 C hypothesised that tau decided the 53/19/44 spread; A tests it and it holds: the same three checkpoints re-order to 85/79/84 when the rule stops truncating the gate at 0.5. "s1 is worse" is (c) contradicted -- s1 is within 6 of the others under sampling. The engine instrument for hogeq is `--gate sample` from here (icebow's threshold band 75/71/71 in §5cs.66 stands as measured but should be re-read under sample before any cross-deck comparison; NOT done). What sampling does NOT establish: that sample is the right DEPLOY rule -- it spends to zero elixir against ghosts that cannot punish; a live opponent can. That is the L62k ruling's open half and stays open.
**D. i=1 half, full hogeq set (a), `refetch/fidelity_hogeq_full.txt`, `y_offset_hogeq.txt`, `handedness_hogeq_full.txt`, `crowns_vs_i.txt`.** Re-fetch DONE: 275/299 in 76 min, every marker `data-i="1"` (24,867 rows), 24 tags skipped after RateLimited pauses (resumable; they run after icebow). Driven (first pass, `corpus_v3_i1/hogeq`): 274 usable tags, 222 ok, 52 failed -- all "card has no native evolution form: 26000043", the same reason and the same count as v3's 52/296. **Winner agreement 145/222 = 65.3% vs v3 162/241 = 67.2%; accept 98.0% vs 98.7%; exact crowns 54.5% vs 56.4%** (§5cs.68's n=64 deficit was noise). Frame: per-card mean y of the rotated half vs the i=0 half, 97 (side, card) pairs, weighted mean dy **0.008 tiles**, every blue card within 0.32 -- the rotation (18-x, 32-y) is exact (a); sum |dLeft| rotation 8.74 vs mirror 9.99 on 97 cards. Two (b) residues: (1) engine ends before the real last play in 116/222 = 52% of rotated matches vs 88/241 = 36.5% (z 3.4); (2) from `battles.csv`, the hogeq halves differ in real 3-crown rate, i0 17.3% (n 300) vs i1 8.1% (n 295), z 3.4, while icebow's halves do not (8.8% vs 8.5%, n 625/612) and win rates match on both decks. So `i` is not a pure coin flip on hogeq -- the §5cs.67 "no battle field predicts it" claim was tested on win/mode/date/rating, not crowns -- and (1) may follow from (2) (fewer real 3-crowns, engine still 3-crowns 12.6%). Neither changes the corpus decision; both are recorded for the icebow half as a second witness.
**E. Trap that cost a re-drive (a).** The chained i=1 drive was launched without `--record-every 20`: its replay files carry `play_frames` but no `frames`, so `pipeline/dataset.py` would have built v4 with 0 WAIT rows from the new half (v4-flawed: wait 23,421 = v3's 23,421 exactly, play 18,743 vs 9,797) -- a play/wait mix change hiding inside a "corpus only" experiment. Build deleted; re-drive with v3's exact flags (`--record-every 20 --record-plays --determinism-every 10`) running on 37032 into `corpus_v3_i1r/hogeq` (165/274 at 11:08 UTC), and the corpus_v4 build + S1 x3 (`s1_v4/run_hogeq_v4.sh`) is chained to its `aggregate.json`.
**F. Tooling (a).** `pipeline/train_s1.py --tag` (checkpoint `s1_<deck>_<tag>_s<seed>.pt`, default unchanged) so v4 runs cannot overwrite the v3 checkpoints the engine reads; `pipeline/eval_s1.py` evaluates any checkpoint on one dataset's val rows -- reproduces `s1_hogeq_s0` at 0.2130 exactly -- so v3 and v4 models are read on the SAME val rows (v4's split keeps v3's val tags and adds i=1 ones; the v3-val read is the like-for-like one). ### §5cs.67 -- L64h (2026-09-06 08:0x-08:3x UTC): **the x/y-less HALF of the crawl is a CRAWLER JOIN BUG, not a property of the battles -- every replay ships placement markers; the ones the crawler dropped carry `data-i="1"` (a per-replay perspective flag) and its join only ever looked up `"0"`. Verified on a fresh fetch (109/109 markers, all i=1). Re-fetch of the 618 icebow + 299 hogeq uncovered replays LAUNCHED with a fixed join; expected positioned corpus 619 -> ~1,237 icebow, 296 -> 595 hogeq (2.0x) before any new crawling. Also: the i=1 half is in the OTHER seat's frame (team median tile_y 13.5 vs 18.5) -- the corpus build must rotate it.**

**A. Why (a), subagent record `L64/xy_why/xy_why.md` (+ `icebow_xy_why.txt`, `hogeq_xy_why.txt`, `*_partials.txt`, scripts).** x/y is all-or-nothing per replay: icebow 619 replays at fraction exactly 1, 612 at exactly 0, 6 with exactly ONE row; hogeq 296 / 295 / 4. No battle-level field separates the halves (pathOfLegend 605/1,201 = 50.4%; win 408/818 vs loss 211/419; every rating bucket 46-53%; every player n>=20 between 38-69%; flat over battle date 2024 -> 2026-09-05, hour, crawl wave, within-player time order; `battles_raw.json` has no extra keys) -- (i) mode and (ii) age/expiry are **contradicted**. The 10 one-row "partials" are the fingerprint: each is the red occurrence-1 row of a same-tick same-card cross-side pair, i.e. the only row whose lookup key was `(t, card, "1")` -- that key EXISTED. `crawl_icebow.py:91/101` (verbatim `crawl_deck.py:117/127`) keys markers on `(data-t, data-c, data-i)` assuming `data-i` is an occurrence index and looks up `"0"` or the occurrence number; `data-i` is a per-replay flag at 50% prevalence.
**Fresh-fetch verification (a), `L64/xy_why/refetch/probe_i1.py`, `markers_i1.txt`:** uncovered tag `00YYPYJ2GPUU` re-fetched through the saved session token (still valid): 109 timeline cards, **109 markers with data-t, ALL `data-i="1"`** (56 red/'o', 53 blue/'t'), x range 0.5-17.5 both sides. The old probe payload (covered `02GY9GQLLQ2Y`): 109/109 markers `data-i="0"`. So the crawler threw away half of what it downloaded, and (the second trap) kept no raw payloads, so nothing could be re-parsed offline.
**B. Frame (a on two payloads, (b) as a rule).** In the i=0 payload the team ('t' = timeline `blue`) sits at tile_y > 16 (93.2%, median 18.5; teslas median 21.0, x-bows 22.5 -- the §5ag frame). In the i=1 payload the team sits at tile_y < 16 (86.8%, median 13.5; teslas 13.0) and the opponent at > 16 (94.3%). `i` therefore marks which seat the stored replay is viewed from: the i=1 half must be brought into the corpus frame by the 180-degree rotation x' = 18 - x, y' = 32 - y (the arena is 180-degree symmetric and a seat swap is a rotation, never a vertical mirror -- a mirror would swap lane handedness). (b) The lane handedness of that rule is untested: the check after the re-fetch is the per-card x histogram of the team's placements, i=0 half vs rotated i=1 half, which must agree (a mirror would flip any left/right asymmetry).
**C. Re-fetch (a, running), `L64/xy_why/refetch/refetch_i1.py`, task bm34pp1cy, icebow then hogeq chained.** Fixed join: markers keyed on `(data-t, data-c, side)` (`data-s` t->blue / o->red, checked: counts match the timeline's 53 blue / 56 red) with in-order pop for repeats; `data-i` stored as `attr_i`. Writes ONLY new files: `<crawl2>/payloads/<tag>.html` (raw payloads kept from now on) and `<crawl2>/plays_ext_i1.csv` (coordinates exactly as served, NO rotation -- the rotation is a corpus-build step so it stays auditable); progress in `refetch/<deck>_done.json`; `plays_ext.csv`, `replays_done.json` untouched. Smoke: 3 replays, 287 rows, 287 with x/y, all i=1, 0 errors. Full run: 615 icebow (3 done) + 299 hogeq; the wave log shows ~10 replays/min before rate limiting, so ~1-1.5 h; RateLimited -> 120 s sleep and continue. No login was needed (saved token accepted at 08:1x UTC).
**D. What this changes.** S2 was scoped as "crawl x3"; half of S2's target is already on disk. After the re-fetch: rebuild corpus_v3 -> v4 with the rotated i=1 half (rotation + the §5ag frame check on the i=1 half as a gate), re-run S1 (same config, 3 seeds per deck, one change = corpus) and read the band against 18.22 +/- 0.11 / 20.99 +/- 0.36 -- the cleanest data-scaling measurement the project can get. The 457 icebow battles in `battles_raw.json` not yet fetched (1,710 raw vs 1,253 done) are a further +457 positioned replays with the same session. Crawler source fix (`crawl_icebow.py`/`crawl_deck.py` in the scraper repo) NOT yet applied -- both files are untracked in that repo; apply before the next wave.
What this does NOT establish: the rotation's handedness (B), the fetched half's frame on more than one payload (the re-fetch summary `i-values` and a per-replay frame check will), and whether RoyaleAPI still serves every one of the 917 tags (refusals are logged per tag).
**TRAPS (a):** (1) `data-i` is a per-replay perspective flag, not an occurrence index -- any consumer of `plays_ext.csv` rows is looking at the i=0 half only, which is a coin-flip sample (no mode/player/date bias measured, so no selection effect on the S1 numbers). (2) The crawler kept no raw payloads; every parser question so far cost a re-fetch. (3) The L64g section and status line were stamped "08:5x UTC" -- commit 3e89c19 is 08:04 UTC; L64g ran 07:3x-08:0x. Clock-label error only.

### §5cs.62 -- L64c (2026-09-06 05:0x-05:2x UTC): **RETRACTION of §5cs.48 (L62i grid ruling -- a unit error: the probe read live-screen FRAME fractions as board tiles; on the trainer's own grid the 432 row pitch IS 1.333 tiles as the owner said, and 576 has ZERO quantisation error on all 2,657 pro x-bows); old IL init re-scored on the S1 val plays (13.70/41.73 on its 432 grid, 6.69% at 1-tile bins); S1 seed 0 icebow: val tile top-1 18.1% / half 15.4% (single seed = screen), gate bal-acc 0.71 with the leak gone; matched-grid read: level with the old init on the 432 grid, ahead on 1-tile bins and on miss distance.**

**A. RETRACTION of §5cs.48 (a).** L62i's probes (`L62/grid_quant_probe*.py`) built the grid with the plain `ActionSpace(cfg)` -- the LIVE tap space, whose `cell_center` returns screen-frame fractions (arena box y 0.137..0.753) -- and converted them with `(1-ny)*32` as if they were board fractions. That is where "row pitch 0.499 tiles, both grids span 19.7 tiles" came from: 0.0156 frame x 32. The trainer, SimMatchEnv and every BC dataset use `clashrl/sim/env.py::_board_action_space` (arena_box [0,0,1,1]); measured through its `cell_center` this loop (`L64/grid_quant_probe_sim.py`, `.out`): **18x24: row pitch 1.333 tiles, col pitch 1.000; 18x32: 1.000 / 1.000.** The live space's 24 rows also span the whole playfield, i.e. 1.333 tiles too -- the "0.499" never existed. Re-run of the quantisation test on the trainer's grid, 2,657 real pro x-bow placements (tile_y median 19.5, on the half-tile lattice): **432: error mean 0.274 tiles, max 0.500, signed dy mean -0.165 (snapped TOWARD the enemy on average), moved back >0.5 tiles 0.0%; 576: error 0.000 mean / 0.000 max** -- the pros' x.5 lattice coincides exactly with the 18x32 cell centres. Reach test (`grid_quant_probe3_sim.py`): 242 in-reach x-bows, **0 pushed out of reach at either grid, worst distance added +0.000**.
So: (i) the owner's 1.333-pitch figure was RIGHT and §5cs.48's contradiction of it is withdrawn; (ii) §5cs.48's claim that 576 "would create the reported failure (55% pushed out of reach)" is withdrawn -- 576 is strictly better (zero snap); (iii) the functional half of the owner's claim ("432 snaps an offensive x-bow one tile back, out of reach") stays contradicted in magnitude: max backward snap is 0.5 tiles and no in-reach x-bow is lost -- (b) the short x-bows observed on engA_kl_m253 were policy error, still untested. Moot for S1 (36x64 half-tile head, exact on the pro lattice by construction), material for the record and for anything still running on the 432 head. TRAP -> §8.

**B. Old init on the S1 val plays (a), subagent record `L64/rescore_old.md`, driver `rescore_old.py`, per-play `rescore_old_preds.npz`.** `bc_bias_native_s0.pt` fed through its own unchanged L61 encoder (`build_bc_v2.assemble_tag` from each corpus_v3 play frame; pro card given, deployable-masked, no gate). Rows align 1:1 with the S1 val play rows (3,796; every (tag, side, tick) matched, pro xy agrees to 5e-5). **432 grid: top-1 13.70 / top-5 41.73** (own v2 val reproduced exactly at 15.00/43.51). 37 of the 85 S1-val replays (1,724 rows) were in the old model's TRAIN split -> **clean 2,072 rows: 13.13 / 41.51**. Per card: x_bow 30.5/75.4, the_log 21.1/52.2, tesla 16.7/56.3, skeletons 9.1/29.3, tornado 6.4/20.8. 175/3,796 pro cells (4.6%) lie outside the old deployable mask (guaranteed misses, the same handicap its 15.00 carried). **1-tile 18x32 bins: top-1 6.69%** (its 1.0 x 1.333 cells straddle tile rows: only 250 of its 520 cell hits survive tile binning); argmax within 1 tile of the pro 14.8%, within 2 tiles 31.3%, mean miss 5.28 tiles.

**C. S1 icebow seed 0 (a), ONE SEED = a screen, `L64/s1/final_icebow_s0.json`, 1,264,680 params, 20 epochs x ~68 s.** Best epoch 14: **val tile top-1 18.12% / half-tile 15.36%** (board-blind baseline 8.90 / 8.48), card 59.2% (baseline 48.1), joint 10.6%, cell NLL 3.86, **gate bal-acc 0.715** (acc 0.786; the leaked run's 0.98 is gone), wait top-1 47.5%, value acc 69.2%, emb cosine 0.20 (old trunk 0.991: the new trunk does NOT collapse its embeddings), train-subset tile 22.4% (4.3 pt train-val gap). Trajectory: tile 16.8% at epoch 8, 18.1 at 14, 17.6 at 16 -- the second half of the schedule added ~1 pt.

**D. Matched-grid read (a), `L64/matched_grid.py` on the seed-0 checkpoint, same 3,796 plays as B.** New argmax half-cell -> xy -> (i) 1-tile bin, (ii) nearest 432 centre. **1-tile: new 17.31% vs old 6.69%** (clean rows 18.48 vs 6.37). **Old's home 432 grid: new 12.54% vs old 13.70%** (clean: 13.61 vs 13.13). Miss distance: new mean 4.07 tiles / median 2.47, within 1 tile 25.9%, within 2 tiles 44.2%; old 5.28 / 4.03, 14.8%, 31.4%. Reading: the 2.6x on tiles is mostly the old head's cell shape; on equal coarseness the two are level (old slightly ahead on all rows, new slightly ahead on the rows the old model never trained on); on how far a miss lands, the new model is clearly better. Instrument note: the trainer's `cell_tile_top1` (18.12) sums the 4 half-cell probabilities per tile before the argmax; matched_grid bins the argmax half-cell (17.31) -- same checkpoint, two readings, quote which.
What this does NOT establish: anything about seeds 1-2 (running), hogeq, the gate under sampling, or engine play. Old-vs-new at the 432 grid is inside one seed's noise until the 3-seed band exists.

### §5cs.61 -- L64b (2026-09-06 04:5x-05:0x UTC): **FIRST S1 RUN DISCARDED -- a ROW-FORMAT LEAK put gate balanced accuracy at 0.98; play frames carried 7-column entities (`kind` -> `deploying` flag) plus `effects`/`projectiles`, the compact wait frames carried neither, so the gate head could read the row TYPE off the token columns. Fixed (`_as_compact` in `pipeline/dataset.py`), both datasets rebuilt (row counts unchanged), 24 tests OK, baselines re-measured identical, 6-seed chain relaunched. Nothing from the leaked run is an S1 result.**

**A. The leak (a).** Diagnosed from the leaked run's own numbers: gate balanced accuracy 0.98 at epoch 1 and flat (`scratchpad/gauntlet/L64/s1/LEAKED_train_icebow_s0.log`, 8 epochs, best val tile top-1 16.8% / half 15.4% / card 59.1% / joint 9.7-10.1% / wait 46-47% / value 70-71% / emb cosine 0.19-0.20; kept as a diagnostic only). Probe (`probe_pf.out` + this loop): play_frames entities are `[side,x,y,name,hp,max_hp,kind]` with kind in {12,13,14,15} (12/14 = deploying -> token cols 8-9 set), compact `frames` entities are the same first 6 columns and no kind; play frames also carry `effects` (-> spell tokens, col 13) and `projectiles`. Token column means BEFORE the fix differed by row type on cols 8, 9, 13; AFTER the fix cols 8-13 are 0.000 for both row types in both decks (icebow play `[0.79,1,0,0,0,0,1,0]` vs wait `[0.777,1,0,0,0,0,1,0]` on cols 6-13; hogeq `0.817` vs `0.804`). What remains different is real state: units/row 5.18 play vs 4.00 wait (icebow), 4.62 vs 3.69 (hogeq); my elixir sc[1] 0.696 vs 0.490 -- pros play when they have elixir, which is what the gate should learn.
Cost of the fix (b): play rows lose the `deploying` flag and in-flight spell effects that the live path DOES provide (from_live sets deploying=None, spells from detector classes) -- the S1 model now never sees a spell token. To restore them without the leak the compact frames would need `record_full`-style effects at every recorded tick (re-drive, ~2.5 h engine time for both decks); parked, listed in §6.
**TRAP (a):** `TaskStop` on a background `bash run_seeds.sh` killed the wrapper shell only -- the script's own bash (2 PIDs) and its python child survived and advanced to seed 1 (verified with `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` by ParentProcessId). Stopping a chain = stop the task, then kill the script's PID tree, then verify `train_s1` count is 0. Same family as the L62h "tree-killing a trainer kills the in-guest worker services" trap, opposite direction.

**B. Rebuild (a).** `python -m pipeline.dataset icebow|hogeq`: icebow 78,277 rows (21,687 play / 56,590 wait / val 13,761 / 493 replays, 14.3 s), hogeq 33,218 (9,797 / 23,421 / 6,133 / 241, 4.6 s) -- identical row counts to §5cs.60 C, only the unit-token columns changed. `unittest pipeline.tests.test_dataset pipeline.tests.test_obs_contract`: 24 OK. Board-blind baselines re-measured on the rebuilt val rows, identical to L64a: icebow tile 8.90% / half 8.48% / card 48.05% (n_val_play 3,796, n_train_play 17,891); hogeq 11.45% / 11.45% / 42.32% (1,817 / 7,980). Leaked checkpoint moved to `scratchpad/gauntlet/L64/s1/leaked_ckpt/s1_icebow_s0.pt` (out of `icebow/data/pipeline/`) so the fresh seed-0 run cannot be confused with it.

**C. Running.** `bash scratchpad/gauntlet/L64/s1/run_seeds.sh` (task b6vmgii7c): icebow s0,s1,s2 then hogeq s0,s1,s2, 20 epochs each, ~71 s/epoch icebow (leaked run's rate) -> ~24 min per icebow seed, hogeq ~10 min -> ETA ~1 h 45 min for all six. Logs `train_<deck>_s<seed>.log`, per-seed `final_<deck>_s<seed>.json`; checkpoints `<deck>/data/pipeline/s1_<deck>_s<seed>.pt`. Timer task armed (560 s). Box: python 3 (nucleo uvicorn + trainer pair), free RAM 6.4 GB before launch.

**D. Next.** Read the three icebow finals when they land (mean +/- band across seeds vs the 8.90% baseline; the old 15.44%/13.65% are a DIFFERENT instrument -- old rows, 432 grid -- until the old trunk is re-scored on these val rows, which is the loop after). Then the S1 gate sanity check: with the leak gone, gate bal-acc should sit well under 0.98; if it is still ~0.98 there is another leak (the elixir gap alone cannot give 0.98 -- (b), testable by a scalar-only gate baseline).

S1 dataset (a), `pipeline/dataset.py`, tests `pipeline/tests/test_dataset.py` (24 OK with the contract tests).** Rows in MY board frame via `from_engine`/`to_tokens`: PLAY rows = the full engine state before every ACCEPTED pro play of a deck-matching side (deck matched on all 8 base keys of `final_decks`; 2 icebow mirror matches give both sides), target = deck slot + continuous (x, y); WAIT rows = every 2nd compact frame (40 ticks = 2 s) with no accepted play in the next 20 ticks, hand/next reconstructed EXACTLY (the engine hand changes only on an accepted play, so between accepted plays k, k+1 the hand is `hand_before(k+1)`), targets = the slot played next + seconds until it. Every row: past-actions channel (last 3 plays: slot, x, y, seconds ago) and the REAL RoyaleAPI crowns (mine, theirs). Split by replay tag (crc32 % 100 < 15 -> val). ### §5cs.54 -- L62m (2026-09-05 22:0x UTC, background task completed unattended; RENUMBERED from
§5cs.52 at 23:2x -- a CONCURRENT SESSION had already claimed §5cs.52/.53 for L63/L63b while this
loop was writing. Two sessions were editing HANDOFF.md at once; see the trap at the end of this section): **THE WAVE-4 CRAWL FINISHED AND THE IMITATION CORPUS IS STILL ONLY ~HALF-USABLE -- 1,253 battles on disk but only 625 (49.9%) carry x/y placement coordinates, and the usable opponent-deck pool is 435, not the 781 the raw battle file suggests.** The owner's bar for the deck pool is >1,000, so the honest gap is 435 -> 1,000, more than double, NOT the "781, nearly there" a naive count gives.

Measured this loop from `icebow/data/royaleapi/crawl2/` (the crawl's own output; no experiment run, box idle).
Crawl log `scratchpad/gauntlet/L61/crawl_icebow_wave4.log`: **"DONE: 565 new replays in 478 min"**, exit 0; the two
crawler processes (29444 / 53824) exited on their own -- the guarded process list is now the owner's uvicorn alone.
(a) unless marked.

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| battles rows | 1,253 |
| replay tags with any plays | 1,237 |
| **replay tags with x/y coordinates** | **625 (49.9%)** |
| play rows total / with x/y | 109,963 / **54,148 (49.2%)** |
| opponent decks, all battles | 781 |
| **opponent decks, USABLE (x/y present)** | **435** |
| usable battles by result | 413 win / 212 loss |

**Why this matters for the next direction.** §5cs.51 ranked "improve the imitation, not the RL" first, and the BC
init that everything failed to beat (15.44/46.61) was fit on ~1,000 pro boards. The corpus can supply more -- 54,148
placement rows now carry coordinates -- but the x/y-less half is the binding constraint on BOTH the board count and
the deck pool, and it has been at ~50% across waves (§5cs.41 recorded the same shape at a smaller scale). **The
cheapest next measurement is not another crawl wave: it is finding out WHY half the replays have no coordinates**
(b -- untested; candidates are the RateLimited errors visible in the log tail, the clearance-renewal path, and a
replay format the parser drops silently). A wave that doubles the battles at the same 50% yield doubles the wasted
half too.

**Not established.** Whether the 565 new replays actually lift the BC fit (untested -- no re-fit was run; the init
on disk is unchanged); whether the x/y-less half is recoverable by a re-parse or needs a re-fetch; whether deck
POOL size or board COUNT is the thing that limits the imitation ceiling (b -- these are different experiments, and
the owner's >1,000 bar is about the pool).

`HANDOFF.md` and `GAUNTLET_LOG.md` and committed. Nothing was lost (this loop's commit `8544985` is verified

but the section number collided and the log blocks are out of order (L62m sits AFTER L63b). Rules for next time:
**(1) before appending a § section, re-read the last section header from disk -- do not trust a number computed
earlier in the loop; (2) never rewrite HANDOFF.md wholesale (read-modify-write) when another session may be live --
append only; a scripted `write_text` would have silently destroyed the other session's work, and in this loop only
an assertion failure prevented exactly that; (3) `git add <named files>` then check `git log --oneline -3` for
commits you did not make before committing.**
